name: Main street, frontier
desc: A trading street at the end of the road, at the hour when the sun is low enough to blind everyone in it.

shots.desc: a frontier trading street of sun-bleached timber storefronts and awninged stalls, crates and produce boxes stacked on the boards, a wooden handcart standing in ochre dust, long shadows thrown the length of the street by a low hard sun, wide shot, no humans
two figures standing either side of a stall counter in the dust, the low sun behind them throwing their shadows the length of the street, full body, wide shot
leaning across the stall counter with one hand flat on the boards, hat brim shading the eyes, dust hanging in the air and catching the low light, medium shot
the stallholder's face under the awning, jaw working, eyes dropping to the counter and coming back up, close-up
coins counted out in a short stack on a scarred wooden counter beside a set of brass scales, ochre dust across the boards, hard low sunlight raking over it, close-up, no humans

why: The western is the largest missing genre in the gallery and the library already has the card for it, hiding under a name that makes it sound like set dressing. It is not: the style card records that western_frontier is really a LIGHT card wearing a genre name, and the low sun and the long shadow do most of the work. So this template gives the light something to fall across. It is deliberately not a duel - duel_standoff already exists and a second one would be a re-run - and the drama is instead the smallest thing the frontier has, a debt being settled at a stall while the light goes. Every camera is static except one push on the line, so the long shadows stay put and the frame never has to re-draw them. The insert is coins on a counter because that is the only shot in the template that says what the scene is about, and because it is an object rather than a face, which means it takes no identity tags and cannot drift.
note: Not rendered. No frame from this template has been generated - the GPU was held for a video job - so everything below is read off the style, place and look cards rather than seen. This style is compose=replaces and it REBUILDS the location on purpose - what was seen was frontier timber buildings, ochre dust and a low hard sun, arriving over whatever place was underneath. Read that as intended here. The place card is not discarded, though: the measured rule is that a place bringing six or more concrete nouns survives and is recoloured, and market_street brings eleven, so the stalls, awnings, crates, handcart and counter should carry through as frontier versions of themselves rather than being deleted. Uncertain and worth watching: this style's negative_add is lush, green, cold, URBAN, MODERN - and negatives are not wired to the renderer, so the two words that would have scrubbed the cobbles and the modern shopfronts will not reach the picture. Expect a frontier market rather than a clean rebuild, and if a cobbled street shows through, that is this gap and not the style failing. Applies to every card in this set and to none of the existing twenty: these templates use place CARDS rather than free text, so the place's own prose is appended to the prompt on top of whatever the shot desc says, and where a desc also names the setting the nouns arrive twice. That is reinforcement rather than contradiction, and it is deliberate on the shots whose place card warns that a particular noun must be named explicitly or the location renders wrong. But if a prompt reads long, the shot desc is the half to trim - never the card. Standing gaps that apply to every card in the gallery: transitions are intent only, because short.py hard-cuts every join regardless of what is set here; every emotion card is status:partial upstream, so the face, eyes, mouth and body tags render and voice_style does not, because no TTS engine on this box takes an emotion vector; and a style's negative_add never reaches the picture, because the renderer has no negative input wired - so this style will come out slightly less clean than its library sample, which had one.
